page: Vultr vbm-4c-32gb is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It is equipped with a dedicated Intel Xeon 1270 processor featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of RAM, which provides 4.0 GB of memory per core, and a 480 GB local SSD. This x86_64 architecture server also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates average performance across standard compute tasks. It achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1728.79 and a multi-core score of 8815.11. Memory performance is highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3192.31, though large-block uncached memory bandwidth tests showed weaker results, with read speeds at 31.11 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.73 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression performed strongly at 30.56 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reached 7.05 GB/sec.

The dedicated bare metal architecture provides resource isolation and consistent performance, making it suitable for general-purpose workloads and moderate database operations. However, the server exhibits performance limitations in highly parallelized or complex computational tasks, as indicated by a weak PassMark CPU physics score of 717.17 and poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks. This hardware profile is best aligned with dedicated web hosting, lightweight database hosting, and general-purpose application environments requiring non-virtualized resources.
